evidence.observation: none: no tenant observation; public docs, OpenAPI documents, the logs schema, W3C and IETF specifications and the pinned MIT SDK only

rules.statement: Passkeys are an authentication method of database connections (strategy auth0) only; a passkey enrollment never touches the password hash or other methods.

authentication_methods.passkey.enabled turns passkeys on; passkey_options holds challenge_ui (both, autofill, button), progressive_enrollment_enabled and local_enrollment_enabled; shapes and defaults unchanged from D-0042 (disabled, both, true, true).
Passkeys are effective only with the new Universal Login experience and Identifier First on; zeroauthy has no classic custom login page (D-0039), so that prerequisite always holds.
Effective only when the connection does not require a username or has flexible identifiers, is not a custom database or has import mode on, and still has passwords enabled (LR33b-2).

The Dashboard blocks saving while a prerequisite is unmet; the Management API behaviour is undocumented, so the API stores any combination and the server offers passkeys only when every prerequisite holds (LR33b-1, W2).
At most 20 passkeys per user, enforced atomically in the store on every create (hosted, native, Management API); hosted error key passkey-enrollment-max-allowed-reached.
password.api_behavior and signup_behavior are stored only; /dbconnections/signup keeps requiring a password (LR33b-3, K8).
Users created through an organization invitation cannot choose a passkey at signup; progressive enrollment covers them later (LR33b-32).
Passwords and passkeys coexist at login; turning passkeys off hides passkeys without deleting them.

A passkey is bound to the RP ID; changing the domain or RP ID makes old passkeys unusable and users re-enroll. Every credential stores its RP ID and ceremonies accept only credentials whose stored RP ID equals the effective RP ID.
The RP ID defaults to the custom domain; CustomDomain.relying_party_identifier (hostname, max 255, any registrable suffix of the domain) overrides it and null falls back to the full domain.
rpid.For resolves per host: the canonical host is its own RP ID; a verified custom domain or operator alias uses its relying_party_identifier, else the host itself (LR33b-4 as amended by R1 and R2).
The Dashboard's tenant-level default RP ID has no Management API; none is built (K5). The console lists every host and its effective RP ID and edits the documented custom-domain field.

An RP ID may be a parent domain so web and native applications share passkeys (R1); security.webauthn.restrict_shared_rp_ids (default false) refuses RP IDs covering the deployment's base domain or another tenant's host for shared hosting.
Security keys and device biometrics use the same RP ID resolver as passkeys: settable only with a custom domain, and a changed custom domain invalidates earlier enrollments.
With multiple custom domains each domain has its own RP ID and its own passkeys and WebAuthn enrollments; users enroll per domain (LR33b-5, K1, K10).

Embedded and native origins must be in the application's Allowed Web Origins; hosted pages accept exactly https://<request host>; origins compare as exact serialized strings and crossOrigin/topOrigin are refused.
When passkeys are effective, login-id gains autocomplete="username webauthn" plus a conditional get for both/autofill and a Continue-with-a-passkey button (passkeyButtonText) for both/button.
If autofill is unavailable the user uses the button (if enabled) or the password; without JavaScript nothing changes on the page.
After a passkey login MFA still applies by default; a post-login Action may skip it; the login continues through Actions, mfa.Decide, consent and organizations exactly as after a password.

login-id error keys passkey-not-allowed, no-passkey, passkey-authentication-failed, invalid-passkey, conflict-password-passkey and password-not-allowed are rendered from the i18n catalog in our own words.

The assertion's credential ID is looked up in the tenant and the credential's user wins over the typed identifier; blocked users get user-blocked; every other failure is the generic passkey-authentication-failed (LR33b-16).

Passkey signup asks for the identifier first (signup-id), then offers a passkey (passkey-enrollment) with a create-a-password alternative (signup-password); the split is used only when passkeys are effective (LR33b-15).

A passkey signup creates the user without a password plus the passkey in one transaction after pre-user-registration; ss carries details.authentication_methods ["passkey"] (password signups ["pwd"]); a passkey-only user's password login fails with the normal wrong-credentials answer (LR33b-36).

Progressive enrollment offers a passkey after an identifier-and-password login when the user has none for the RP ID; skippable; the user may delay it every 30 days; default on; offered after MFA and before consent (LR33b-13).

Local enrollment offers a passkey on the new device after a login with a cross-device passkey (authenticatorAttachment cross-platform) when a user-verifying platform authenticator exists; skippable; default on; don't-show-again snoozes 30 days per user per browser (LR33b-14).
Enrollment screens show only where WebAuthn works; the page script auto-continues (skip, no snooze) when PublicKeyCredential or the platform check is missing.

A successful progressive or local enrollment logs gd_enrollment_complete with details.authenticator.type passkey; a failure logs gd_webauthn_enrollment_failed with details.authentication_methods ["passkey"].

Enrollment is bound to the hosted transaction, its browser cookie and CSRF token and is reachable only after every factor the login required; back or refresh after completion shows the session-expired page.

Client data must be UTF-8 JSON with the ceremony type, a constant-time-equal challenge, an origin from the exact allowed list, crossOrigin absent or false and topOrigin absent; tokenBinding is ignored.

authData is at least 37 bytes with rpIdHash equal to SHA-256 of the RP ID, UP set, UV set when required, AT set on registration, BS without BE rejected, extensions parsed with the bounded decoder and ignored, attested credential data parsed exactly with no unparsed tail.
pubKeyCredParams are -8, -7, -257 in that order; registration accepts only those; assertions also verify -35, -36 and -37 keys imported through the Management API (LR33b-11).

attestation none is requested; format none needs an empty attStmt; packed, tpm, android-key, android-safetynet, fido-u2f and apple are accepted without verifying the statement and recorded as none; unknown formats are rejected; no AAGUID policy (LR33b-9).

If the stored or received sign count is non-zero the received count must be greater, else the assertion is rejected with reason sign_count; synced passkeys report 0 and pass; the store applies the update conditionally (LR33b-10, K14).
BE must equal the stored value (a change is rejected, reason backup_eligibility); BS may change and is written back as credential_backed_up.
Discoverable (passkey first-factor) assertions require a user handle equal to the stored one; MFA assertions with an allow list accept a missing handle and check it when present.

Bounded CBOR subset: integers, byte and text strings, arrays, maps, false/true/null; no tags, floats, indefinite lengths or undefined; duplicate keys and trailing bytes rejected; depth 16, 1024 items, attestation 64 KiB, clientDataJSON 16 KiB, credential ID 1023 bytes, COSE key 16 KiB (LR33b-34).

COSE keys: OKP Ed25519 (-8); EC2 P-256 (-7), P-384 (-35), P-521 (-36) with points checked on curve; RSA (kty 3) -257 and -37 with a 2048-8192-bit modulus and an odd exponent above 1; private-key labels rejected.

Passkey registration uses residentKey required and userVerification preferred with no attachment; passkey login uses userVerification preferred and an empty allowCredentials; rp.name equals rp.id; the UV flag is not required for passkeys (LR33b-8).

user.id is a server-generated handle (32 random bytes per user, reused across that user's passkeys, LR33b-7); user.name is the highest-precedence identifier; user.displayName is name when set, else that identifier.

Challenges are 32 random bytes, single use by conditional update; hosted lifetime 5 minutes (timeout 300000) bound to tenant, transaction, cookie hash, purpose, RP ID, origin and user; native timeout 60000 with the row expiring 10 s later, addressed by an opaque auth_session stored hashed; a failed verification consumes the challenge (LR33b-6, W12).

Prompt and screen names are Auth0's (login-id, passkeys/passkey-enrollment, passkeys/passkey-enrollment-local, mfa-webauthn/*, mfa/mfa-detect-browser-capabilities, reset-password/reset-password-mfa-webauthn-*-challenge); the /u/ paths are local (LR33b-37); every text key gets an English catalog entry in our own words.

One in-tree script inlined with the existing CSP nonce reads JSON options, uses conditional mediation for autofill, posts the credential JSON in a hidden form field (no fetch) and reports only a DOMException name from a fixed set; no CSP or Permissions-Policy relaxation.

Security keys have a user-verification setting Never (default), If supported or Required mapping to discouraged, preferred and required; FIDO-1 keys fail when Required; the setting is stored in Guardian settings and exposed through an extension system route (LR33b-22, K6).

Device biometrics cannot be the only factor: the API accepts enabled true alone but the factor is offered only to a user who already has another confirmed enforced factor; the console warns (LR33b-20, K4).

Biometrics are enrolled through progressive device enrollment after another factor, one device per class (phone, tablet, desktop), with Continue, Remind me later (14 days), Not on this device (365 days) and Not now (LR33b-18).
Device recognition is by user agent: per operating system on Windows and iOS 14.5+, per browser on macOS, Chrome only on Android (LR33b-19).

Browsers without JavaScript or WebAuthn are not offered WebAuthn; mfa-detect-browser-capabilities runs before the factor list whenever a WebAuthn factor could be offered and no result means unavailable; the user gets another factor or the recovery code.
Usable WebAuthn authenticators are filtered by RP ID before mfa.Decide; a user whose only factors are credentials for another RP ID is sent to enrollment.

WebAuthn challenge failures count in Plan 33's per-user per-factor throttle (10 per 15 minutes, too-many-webauthn-challenge-attempts-error); passkey login failures count only in the general limiter and the R3 attack-protection rules (LR33b-30).

After roaming registration the key is named on mfa-webauthn-change-key-nickname, 1-20 characters (OpenAPI name maxLength 20, minimum 1 local); platform enrollments get a default name and the platform texts (LR33b-31).
WebAuthn challenge screens carry rememberMeText and remember-browser works as for OTP.

challengeWith, challengeWithAny, enrollWith and enrollWithAny accept webauthn-roaming and webauthn-platform; api.multifactor.enable any and guardian include enabled WebAuthn factors; an explicit platform enroll still needs another confirmed factor first.
Enrollment tickets accept factor webauthn-roaming and webauthn-platform (GuardianEnrollmentFactorEnum).
The MFA API lists and removes WebAuthn enrollments but cannot enroll them; their authenticator_type is the factor name; associate and challenge refuse; passkeys never appear (LR33b-21, W7).
password-reset-post-challenge with a WebAuthn factor renders the same pages under reset-password-mfa-webauthn-platform-challenge and reset-password-mfa-webauthn-roaming-challenge.

The client must list urn:okta:params:oauth:grant-type:webauthn in grant_types, be first party and OIDC conformant; otherwise /passkey/* answer 400 invalid_request and /oauth/token unauthorized_client.
Requests must be made on a custom domain; the default domain is rejected: the canonical host answers 400 invalid_request, operator alias hosts serve the APIs (LR33b-25, R2).

/passkey/register takes client_id, client_secret (client_secret_post), realm, organization, user_profile (email, phone_number, username, name 1-300, given_name 1-150, family_name 1-150, nickname 1-300, picture) and user_metadata (up to 10 string fields); unknown user_profile keys are invalid_request.
user_profile must carry every identifier required at signup; an existing user under any submitted identifier fails with invalid_request (documented, rate limited by the registration budget, R3).
Native registration is unsupported when SMS or email OTP verification is required at signup on the connection: 400 invalid_request.

realm omitted means the tenant's default directory when it is a database connection enabled for the client, else the client's only enabled database connection with passkeys effective, else 400 invalid_request; organization follows the Plan 29 password-realm rules.

/passkey/register returns {auth_session, authn_params_public_key{challenge, timeout, rp{id,name}, user{id,name,displayName}, pubKeyCredParams, authenticatorSelection{residentKey required, userVerification preferred}}}; /passkey/challenge returns {auth_session, authn_params_public_key{challenge, timeout, rpId, userVerification preferred}}.

400 invalid_request, 401 invalid_client, 404 {"error":"not_found"} when the store lacks webauthn.v1 or no database connection has passkeys effective (K9, no tenant flag), 429 too_many_requests from the general limiter; passkey_challenge_started and passkey_challenge_failed are logged with details.purpose.

POST /oauth/token with grant_type urn:okta:params:oauth:grant-type:webauthn, client_id, client authentication, auth_session, authn_response (a JSON object, or a JSON string in a form body as @auth0/auth0-auth-js 1.16.1 sends), optional realm, scope, audience and organization; auth_session is consumed first (single use, same client, realm and organization).

A register auth_session verifies the registration, runs pre-user-registration, creates the user without a password plus the passkey in one transaction, logs ss with authentication_methods ["passkey"] and runs post-user-registration.

A login auth_session verifies the assertion against the credential found by ID in the tenant (user handle required); a blocked user is invalid_grant; then Actions (event.transaction.protocol oauth2-webauthn, passkey in event.authentication.methods), mfa.Decide with mfa_required, refresh tokens by the normal rules and log s with performed_amr ["phr"].

Missing parameters are 400 invalid_request; an expired, consumed or mismatched auth_session and every verification failure are 400 invalid_grant with a fixed description (LR33b-25, D-0061 addendum); each failure logs passkey_challenge_failed; the grant is not advertised in discovery.
MFA grants that follow a passkey mfa_token log sepkotpft, sepkoobft and sepkrcft; those that follow a password mfa_token log seotpft, seoobft and sercft through the same dispatch (LR33b-28).

A native or embedded ceremony accepts https://<request host>, any https origin whose host equals the RP ID or a subdomain of it and is listed in the client's web_origins, and android:apk-key-hash:<base64url SHA-256> for each configured Android fingerprint (LR33b-26).

Client mobile (ios.team_id, ios.app_bundle_identifier, android.app_package_name, android.sha256_cert_fingerprints) is stored and returned, validated against ClientMobile, ClientMobileiOS and ClientMobileAndroid (D-0039 addendum).

Each verified custom domain and operator alias serves /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (webcredentials apps <team_id>.<bundle_id>) and /.well-known/assetlinks.json (delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds) from first-party clients holding the passkey grant and matching mobile fields; 404 when none; not on the canonical host (LR33b-27).

event.authentication.methods includes {name: passkey, timestamp} when the session's first factor was a passkey, and (K11, pulled forward from Plan 40) pwd, federated, email and sms from the session record; mfa follows with its factor type.
event.user.enrolledFactors lists webauthn-roaming and webauthn-platform; passkeys are not MFA factors and are not listed (LR33b-12).
event.transaction.protocol is oauth2-webauthn for the passkey grant (also in the Plan 32 event catalog internal/eventrules/catalog.json).
Logs record performed_amr ["phr"]; nothing documents an ID token amr for passkeys, so a passkey alone leaves amr unchanged and MFA still yields ["mfa"] (K7, LR33b-12, W10).
The MCD page's sample Action checks method.name === "webauthn", a name documented nowhere else; it is not emitted (K13).
pre-user-registration and post-user-registration run for passkey signups (hosted and native) as for password signups.

gd_webauthn_enrollment_failed, gd_webauthn_challenge_failed, passkey_challenge_started, passkey_challenge_failed, sepkotpft, sepkoobft, sepkrcft, seotpft, seoobft and sercft move from deferred to emitted with owner Plan 33b; gd_auth_rejected (push decline) is not planned.

s carries details.prompts[{name login-id, performed_amr ["phr"]}]; ss details.authentication_methods; gd_enrollment_complete details.authenticator.type; gd_webauthn_* authentication_methods or authenticator, first_factor (true for hosted passkey logins, LR33b-17) and failure_details.errorCode; passkey_challenge_* purpose and error.message (W8).

The key-name scrubber gains authn_response, auth_session, attestationObject, authenticatorData, clientDataJSON, signature, userHandle, user_handle and challenge_id; no log, event, Action event or console response carries client data, attestation, signatures, sessions, challenges or user handles.
user.updated fires when the derived multifactor changes; passkey create, delete, sign-count, BS and last_auth_at updates fire nothing; passkey signups emit user.created (LR33b-33).

A passkey authentication method lists id, type passkey, name, created_at, last_auth_at, key_id, public_key, relying_party_identifier, credential_device_type (multi_device iff BE), credential_backed_up (BS), aaguid, identity_user_id, user_agent, user_handle and transports; IDs are passkey|dev_<20 alphanumerics> (W1).

POST type passkey (CreatedUserAuthenticationMethodTypeEnum) requires key_id and a valid COSE public_key; relying_party_identifier defaults to the default custom domain's RP ID else the canonical host; identity_user_id defaults to the user's database identity; user_handle defaults to the existing handle; the 21st passkey is 400 invalid_body and a duplicate key_id in the tenant 409; needs webauthn.v1 else 501 webauthn_unavailable (LR33b-23, LR33b-29, W3).

DELETE /users/{id}/authentication-methods and PUT keep passkeys (documented as enrolled MFA factors); DELETE /users/{id}/authenticators, GET enrollments and multifactor exclude passkeys and include WebAuthn factors (W9).
The usage guide shows camelCase keys for a webauthn-roaming method; the OpenAPI uses snake case, which zeroauthy keeps (K3).
Linking moves the secondary user's passkeys to the primary unchanged (identity_user_id keeps the secondary identity); unlinking moves them back; user deletion deletes passkeys (LR33b-24, W11).

GET/PUT /guardian/factors webauthn-roaming and webauthn-platform move from stored to enforced; the security-key user-verification setting lives in GuardianSettings.Stored["webauthn-roaming/settings"] with a marked extension route.
GET /api/system/tenants/{tenant}/connections/{id}/passkey-prerequisites returns {effective, unmet[]} for the console; connections keep their wire shape.

LoginSession records AuthMethods [{name, type, at}] with SessionAuthenticationSignal names (pwd, passkey, federated, email, sms, mfa with the factor type); the session view returns them and legacy sessions keep pwd.

gRPC stores negotiate webauthn.v1 separately and latched like phone.v1; without it passkey options stay stored-only, WebAuthn factors are not offered, native endpoints answer 404, Management API passkey create answers 501 and mobile stays ignored.

Migration 0035_webauthn.sql adds sessions.auth_methods, clients.mobile and webauthn_snoozes (kinds passkey-progressive, passkey-local, platform-remind, platform-refuse); credentials stay in mfa_authenticators with the per-tenant credential uniqueness; expiring challenges and snoozes join the purge sweep.
The pinned MIT SDK's PasskeyClient.register, challenge and getTokenByPasskey define the request shapes exercised in acceptance; it sends authn_response as a JSON string in a form body.
The passkeys prompt partial group is stored only (LR33b-35); webauthn_platform_first_factor stays stored for Plan 44 (K12).

passkey-register.credentials: exclude: the user's credentials for the RP ID (none on signup)

passkey-register-local.credentials: exclude: the user's credentials for the RP ID

webauthn-roaming.credentials: the user's roaming credentials for the RP ID

webauthn-platform.credentials: the user's platform credentials for the RP ID

log_codes.s: Hosted passkey login succeeded: details.prompts[{name: login-id, performed_amr: [phr]}]; the native grant logs the same on success.
log_codes.ss: Hosted or native passkey signup created the user: details.authentication_methods [passkey].
log_codes.gd_enrollment_complete: Progressive or local passkey enrollment (authenticator.type passkey) or a WebAuthn MFA enrollment (authenticator.type = factor) succeeded.
log_codes.gd_webauthn_enrollment_failed: A passkey enrollment failed (authentication_methods [passkey], failure_details.errorCode) or a WebAuthn MFA enrollment failed (authenticator.type, failure_details).
log_codes.gd_webauthn_challenge_failed: A hosted passkey login assertion failed (first_factor true, LR33b-17) or a WebAuthn MFA challenge failed (first_factor false, authenticator, failure_details).
log_codes.passkey_challenge_started: A native /passkey/register or /passkey/challenge call issued a challenge (details.purpose register or login).
log_codes.passkey_challenge_failed: A native challenge was refused or a passkey grant verification failed (details.purpose, error.message with a bounded reason).
log_codes.sepkotpft: An mfa-otp grant completed after a passkey mfa_token.
log_codes.sepkoobft: An mfa-oob grant completed after a passkey mfa_token.
log_codes.sepkrcft: An mfa-recovery-code grant completed after a passkey mfa_token.
log_codes.seotpft: An mfa-otp grant completed after a password mfa_token (LR33b-28).
log_codes.seoobft: An mfa-oob grant completed after a password mfa_token (LR33b-28).
log_codes.sercft: An mfa-recovery-code grant completed after a password mfa_token (LR33b-28).
log_codes.gd_auth_failed: A WebAuthn MFA challenge did not validate (Plan 33 rule, unchanged).
log_codes.gd_auth_rejected: Not planned: push decline needs Auth0's Guardian app.
